newsitem.title: UK: Conservatives will stand by Major - poll.
newsitem.headline: Conservatives will stand by Major - poll.

text.p: Twenty-seven percent of Conservatives want Prime Minister John Major to continue as head of the party if he loses the general election, according to a poll published on Friday.

A MORI poll for The Economist showed that Major with 27 percent support was well ahead of Deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine with 16 percent and former leader Margaret Thatcher who had 13 percent.
MORI questioned 1,800 people for the survey from September 20-23.

In another poll in the same magazine, 75 Conservative Party candidates in relatively safe seats said they regarded themselves as so-called Eurosceptics, reluctant to forge closer ties with the European Union.
Not one of the candidates supported a single European currency. They also favoured the restoration of the death penalty by three to one.
